card.occupation: Site operations manager at a third-party logistics distribution centre near Alconbury, responsible for about 180 warehouse staff across three shifts
card.education_detail: Left school in St Neots with GCSEs and two A-levels (Business Studies and PE, mediocre grades). Started as a temp picker at 19, made shift supervisor at 23, and later did a part-funded CMI Level 5 in Management and Leadership through work. She never finished the written assignments on time but got through.
card.household: Lives with her husband Craig, 41, a self-employed electrician, in a four-bed new-build on an estate on the edge of Huntingdon. They have one son, Alfie, aged 9, and a cockapoo called Biscuit. Craig does most of the school runs because Gemma's hours are unpredictable.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Cambridgeshire. Her dad was a lorry driver and her mum worked in a school kitchen. She was brought up without religion and doesn't think about it. She is the first in her family to be on a salary like hers and is quietly proud of that, though she would never say so in those words.
card.professional_persona: Direct, fast and short-tempered. She is good in a crisis: a missed trailer, an agency no-show, a client screaming about peak volumes. She is much worse at the steady paperwork side. Her inbox runs into the thousands, she forgets one-to-ones, and she leans heavily on her deputy, Priya, to keep the KPIs reporting and the audits tidy. Staff see her as fair but harsh. She doesn't sugar-coat, she has little patience for excuses, and she will tell a team leader in front of others that something is 'not good enough'. Her 50-60 hour weeks come more from firefighting than from planning.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in any committed way. She used to play netball at school and has a gym membership she uses in fits and starts, usually after a comment about her weight or a holiday booking. She watches the football if Craig has it on (he supports Arsenal) but isn't fussed. She walks Biscuit round Hinchingbrooke Country Park at weekends.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest. She watches telly in the evenings: Gogglebox, Married at First Sight, the odd true-crime documentary, and whatever series everyone at work is talking about. She has been to a couple of musicals in London for hen dos and birthdays and enjoyed the drinks more than the show. She doesn't read books beyond a holiday paperback.
card.travel_persona: One big summer holiday a year, ideally somewhere hot and all-inclusive: Tenerife, Turkey, once Cancún. She likes a pool, a sunbed and not having to organise anything. Weekend breaks to Center Parcs with Alfie. Craig books everything because she leaves it too late. She has no real interest in sightseeing or 'finding the authentic bit'.
card.culinary_persona: Doesn't enjoy cooking and doesn't pretend to. Weeknight dinners are whatever Craig throws together, a ready meal, or a takeaway on Fridays (usually Indian or a Chinese from the place on the high street). She likes a roast at her mum's on Sundays. She drinks rosé or a gin and tonic and has a steady habit of coffee from the vending machine at work.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching reality TV with a glass of wine
Occasional nights out with old school friends in St Neots
Scrolling Facebook Marketplace for things she doesn't need
Following her son's football team on Saturday mornings, mostly from the car with a coffee
skills: Handling difficult clients and agency suppliers
Making quick operational decisions under pressure
Warehouse management systems and labour planning (at a practical level)
Holding people to account, sometimes too bluntly
card.career_goals: Wants to be a general manager running a bigger site, or a regional ops role, mainly for the money and so she doesn't have to answer to her current GM, whom she thinks is useless. She has no plan for how to get there beyond 'keep the numbers up and apply when something comes up'. She has turned down a move to Daventry because she won't relocate.
card.voice: Mid-pace, slightly clipped, a fairly neutral south-east Midlands/East Anglian accent with dropped t's ('a lo' of'). Says 'dinner' for her evening meal, and 'mum'. Uses 'erm' when she's thinking and 'sort of' a fair bit, and ends points with 'yeah?' or 'you know'. She is blunt and will answer a question she finds silly with a flat 'Not really' or 'Dunno, never thought about it.' She doesn't fill silences to be nice; she waits for the next question or says 'Is that it?' She can be dryly funny, usually at someone else's expense, and says 'knackered' a lot.
card.typing: Quick and careless. Mostly lowercase, drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im'), few full stops, and runs sentences together with commas. She uses 'tbh' and 'idk' and the occasional 'lol' when she's being sarcastic. Short answers, often a single line, and she won't go back to fix typos.
card.with_strangers: Polite enough on the surface but impatient. She wants to know what this is and how long it'll take. She can come across as cold or a bit dismissive at first, and doesn't do much small talk or warm agreement. Once she's decided you're not wasting her time she relaxes slightly and gets chattier, mostly complaining about work.
small_things: The dog has chewed another charging cable
Peak season at work is 'a nightmare every year, without fail'
Alfie's football kit always being muddy and never washed in time
Being knackered after a run of night-shift cover
deeper_things: She feels like a worse mum than Craig and gets defensive about it
She knows people at work don't really like her and tells herself she doesn't care
Her dad's health has been going downhill, and she hasn't visited as much as she should
She sometimes wonders whether the long hours are really worth it, then shuts the thought down
She and Craig argue about money even though they're comfortable
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the shot looks a little up at her chin. She's sitting at the kitchen island in the evening under bright overhead spotlights, with a slightly cold white cast. Head and shoulders are framed slightly off-centre to the left. She has a round face with light make-up worn off from the day, a faint frown and a flat, unimpressed expression with one eyebrow slightly raised. Her shoulder-length highlighted blonde hair is scraped back into a low claw clip, with darker roots showing. She wears a navy quarter-zip fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest, and no glasses. Behind her are grey gloss kitchen cabinets, a black kettle and a toaster, a half-full glass of rosé on the counter, a stack of post and a school letter held by a magnet on the American-style fridge, and the edge of a dog bed on the floor with part of a brown cockapoo visible.
